abstract: The existing card based parking system at shopping malls requires staff to hand out parking cards, makes customers search for free slots by themselves, and only reveals parking fees at the exit gantry. This project proposes M-parking, a mobile application for Android phones with NFC that lets members check in and check out by tapping their phone at the gantry. The system recommends a parking zone based on the store the customer wants to visit or the first available zone from the lowest floor upward, and members can view their parking time and fees during the session. A web application lets the administrator manage customers, staff, zones, slots, stores, floor plans, and parking rates, and produce daily and monthly parking reports. The proposed system is analyzed and designed using data flow diagrams, an entity relationship diagram, and a data dictionary.

Thailand has many websites with game news and ratings but none that gathers game promotions in one place, so gamers miss limited time deals and must search each game company site themselves. This project built a game promotion website where visitors and members can browse games, view promotion details, and read game news. Members can rate games on graphics, audio, and gameplay, write comments, and subscribe to games to receive notification of new promotions. Administrators manage games, promotions, and member accounts through the backend. The website is developed in PHP with a MySQL database.

canonical_title: MIDI Signals Manipulating Console for Live Multiple-Keyboard Performance
abstract: Nowadays, music concerts or live performances need good music equipment especially ones that make the performance turn out entertaining for the audience, have its unique point, and multiple keyboards is one of the most important equipment. Keyboard-type device that doesn't have a built-in sound source is called a MIDI controller. There are two types of MIDI controllers: performance controllers that generate notes and are used to perform music, and controllers that may not send notes, but transmit other types of real-time events. Many devices are some combination of the two types. Keyboard-type device needs to be connected to other devices that are the source of the sound, through MIDI protocol. Yet, existing musical instrument digital interfaces are designed for sound engineers, which are not easy to use for real-time performance by musicians of typical instruments, even by pianists. In this project, we studied the technologies involved with modern digital sound productions, then created an easy and futuristic musical instrument as a digital interface for multiple keyboards that supports live music performance, is not more complicated to operate than an organ, and utilizes a potentially unlimited repertoire of sounds.

In 2020, the whole world is facing one of the most extreme contagious diseases which is Covid-19. Covid-19 can easily spread from people to people through the droplets from nose or mouth when the patient coughs or sneezes, or even touches their faces after touching the surface that has been covered by the droplets. With the loss of protection, more than 20 million people got infected from the Covid-19. Therefore, every country is trying to persuade everyone to wear a mask to avoid the spread of the Covid-19. In Thailand, the government set the regulation that everyone must wear masks in the public area, the same with stores and shops around the country. Hence, many public places like shopping malls, convenience stores and restaurants, need to have employees to check every customer that intends to enter the store whether they're wearing a mask or not which increases costs for labour or loss labour to do other tasks. In consequence, we arose an idea of the mask detector to help the store's owner lower the cost and be able to manage the employees efficiently. Our product is a mask detector which uses the video stream from a webcam to detect the faces of the customer entering into the store and detect whether they are wearing masks or not.

For Vincent Mary School of Science and Technology students about to enroll in senior project 1 and 2, it can sometimes be difficult to understand what these projects are about or how they work. Most of the students are clueless about what kind of project to make or which advisor to choose. That is the main problem that we're going to solve in this senior project. As a solution, we will build a platform for end users to view senior projects easily and have detailed information about certain projects and advisors. A recommendation algorithm to help suggest some projects that might be useful for them when deciding on a senior project topic. For our senior project, our system will be able to recommend projects, showcase past projects as well as provide useful information about advisors.

canonical_title: My portfolio: Web Application for Portfolio Builder
aliases: My portfolio: Web Application for Resume Builder
abstract: A resume is a one-page summary of your professional experience, whether it is new or has been ongoing for some time (two pages only under special circumstances). It highlights the jobs you've done and presently hold, the responsibilities you've taken on, the talents you've developed, and the traits you bring to the table, just like a portfolio does. My portfolio is an online application that allow for the creation of an individual's resume or portfolio. The method is simple to use, and it eliminates the need to think about and build a CV based on qualifications. The method was designed to make creating a creative-looking resume to a professional-looking resume straightforward for people of all ages, from children to adults. Individuals must simply fill out a form that includes questions from the default required fields, such as personal questions, educational questions, qualities, interests, and abilities. Users' responses are saved, and the system automatically generates a well-structured resume based on the template selected by the user. Users can create resumes in the PDF format.

This project aims to develop a web application that offers a virtual guide to a university campus through a series of 360-degree videos, with the goal of enhancing the University's attractiveness and international reputation. The web application will be designed to provide an engaging user experience, and its content will be organized into categories that can be managed by an appointed admin user through a Content Management System (CMS). The virtual guide will be built using cutting-edge technology such as Next.js, MongoDB, NextAuth, Bootstrap, Material UI, and a CDN. The report will detail the development process, system design, and implementation of the virtual guide web application, along with potential future improvements and expansions. The project's scope and limitation will be discussed, with an emphasis on using Vimeo or YouTube as a CDN to host and stream 360-degree videos. The report will also cover the framework and methodology used to develop the web application, including the frontend development using Next.js, backend development using Node.js API routes, database management using MongoDB, video CDN integration, and authentication implementation using NextAuth.

canonical_title: AU CANTEEN: AU Student Food Ordering Platform
advisor: Asst. Prof. Dr. Anilkumar Kothalil Gopalakrishnan
abstract: Campus dining is important for daily life of university students. However, many students still find it difficult to explore food options on campus. At Assumption University, there is currently no main platform where students can easily view the information about canteen shops, menus, prices, or opening hours. Because of this, students, especially new students often need to walk around the canteen area to see what food is available. This can take time and may cause confusion when trying to decide what to eat. During busy hours, this situation can also contribute to long queues. To improve this problem, this project develops the AU Canteen System, which is a web-based platform designed to help students explore food options in the campus canteen more easily. Through the system, students can browse different shops, check menus and prices, and see available food before going to the canteen. Having this information online allows students to decide what they want in advance and can help reduce waiting time during peak periods. The platform uses a role-based structure with three types of users: students, shop owners, and administrators. Students can browse menus and place orders through a simple interface. Shop owners have access to a dashboard where they can manage their menus, receive orders, and update the status of each order. Administrators manage the overall system and monitor important data to ensure the platform operates properly. The AU Canteen System is developed using several web technologies. The front-end is built with Next.js, which helps create an interactive and responsive user interface. The backend services are implemented using Node.js APIs. PostgreSQL, hosted on Neon, is used for storing system data, while Cloudinary is used to store and manage all the food images and transaction receipts. User authentication is handled using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) to ensure secure access. The application is deployed on Vercel, allowing users to access the system online. In summary, the AU Canteen System provides a centralized platform that improves access to canteen information and supports better food discovery. By organizing menus, shop information, and ordering functions in one system, the platform helps make the campus dining experience more convenient and efficient for everyone.

canonical_title: AU Timeout: Sports Court Booking and Equipment Rental System for Assumption University
abstract: The rapid advancement of mobile technology and cloud computing has significantly transformed the way organizations manage operational processes. In educational institutions, digital solutions are increasingly adopted to improve administrative efficiency and enhance user experience. At Assumption University, the current sports court booking and equipment rental process is primarily manual or semi-digital, resulting in inefficiencies, scheduling conflicts, limited transparency, and increased administrative workload. This senior project presents the design and development of AU Timeout, a centralized iOS mobile application developed to digitalize sports court reservations and equipment rental management for Assumption University students. The system enables students to check real-time court availability, book sports facilities, rent sports equipment (including both free and paid items), and manage booking history directly through a mobile application. In addition, a matchmaking feature is introduced, allowing students to create sports matches for specific activities and enabling other users to join, thereby promoting community engagement and organized sports participation. The system includes an administrative web-based dashboard that allows staff members to manage courts, set equipment pricing, monitor bookings and rentals, and track revenue. The backend infrastructure is implemented using Firebase services, including Firebase Authentication for secure user login, Firebase Firestore as a real-time cloud database, and Firebase Hosting for web deployment. The system architecture ensures real-time synchronization, scalability, and secure data management. The system is developed using Firebase services including Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore to provide secure user management, real-time data synchronization, and scalable cloud-based storage. The implementation of AU Timeout transforms a manual operational process into a structured digital system, improving efficiency, reducing human error, and enhancing transparency. The proposed solution contributes to the digital transformation initiative of Assumption University and supports the development of a smart campus environment.

The Rangoon QR Ordering System is a web-based digital solution developed for Rangoon Food House, a Burmese restaurant that serves authentic Myanmar cuisine. The system aims to improve the restaurant ordering process by utilizing QR code technology, allowing customers to scan a QR code at their table to access the menu, place orders, and interact with the system directly through their mobile devices. The system provides two main interfaces: a customer interface and an admin interface. Customers can browse menu items, view prices in Thai Baht, customize orders, and choose between dine-in or takeaway options. In addition, the system includes features such as order history and a waiter call function, which sends a notification sound to staff when assistance is requested. On the admin side, the system enables staff to manage menu items, monitor and update orders in real time, and view order history with filtering options. It also includes a dashboard that provides insights into daily sales, total revenue, and popular menu items to support better decision-making. The system is developed using modern web technologies, including React.js for the frontend, Laravel (PHP) for the backend, and MySQL for the database. By implementing this system, Rangoon Food House can enhance service efficiency, reduce waiting time, minimize human errors, and improve the overall customer dining experience.

This project is about the development of Jewelry Shop Management System, which is intended for the operation and management of the daily activities of a jewelry business. The system assists in managing significant business information such as customers, products, invoices, purchases, vendors, promotions, and material sources. The organization and storage of such information using the system are expected to improve data accuracy, efficiency, and transparency for the operation and management of the business. Using the Jewelry Shop Management System, users are able to manage products, inventory, customers' purchases, and vendors' buyback. Additionally, the system is also used for price management using gold price history and promotion discounts. The structure of the system is based on a relational database design that connects different entities such as products, customers, invoices, and vendors. Using the Jewelry Shop Management System, the operation and management of a jewelry business are expected to be more effective and efficient for the owners and managers. In particular, the system is expected to help the owners and managers monitor products, sales, and customers in a more systematic and reliable manner. In essence, the project is about the potential benefits and advantages of using information systems and database technologies for the operation and management of the jewelry retail industry.

canonical_title: Game Realism through Graphics and Physics
abstract: The development of visually realistic virtual environments has become an important objective in modern computer graphics and game development. Game engines such as Unreal Engine 5 provide advanced technologies for real-time rendering and physics simulation, enabling developers to create highly immersive environments. However, achieving high levels of realism in real-time applications introduces significant computational challenges. Rendering systems that simulate realistic lighting behavior require substantial GPU resources, while physics simulation systems require CPU processing power. Because real-time applications must maintain stable frame rates, rendering and physics systems must operate within strict performance constraints. Indoor environments present additional challenges because lighting reflections and object interactions occur within confined spaces. Small visual artifacts or unstable physics behavior can significantly reduce perceived realism. Developers must therefore carefully balance rendering quality and physics precision to achieve both visual fidelity and performance stability. This project investigates the interaction between rendering and physics subsystems in Unreal Engine 5 and proposes a performance-aware framework for enhancing indoor scene realism. The study analyzes how rendering technologies such as Lumen global illumination and physics systems such as the Chaos physics engine compete for computational resources within a fixed frame-time budget. The results suggest that improvements in lighting coherence often produce greater perceptual realism benefits than marginal increases in physics precision in typical indoor scenes. Based on this observation, a system-level framework is proposed that coordinates rendering and physics parameters to optimize realism while maintaining real-time performance.
